summary: Verified diagnostic + name-based matching changes to the DocGalaxy autofill bookmarklet end-to-end against the local mock harness. Admin login (ashokashok7751@gmail.com / DocGalaxy@2026) succeeded, 'View & Bookmarklet' dialog opens, 'Copy Code' button is present. Decoded the javascript: href for order 96a6aa44-988d-4e50-bb48-bb53850e4a7f and confirmed: (a) NO 'alert(' substring, (b) autofill endpoint '/api/orders/<id>/autofill' is embedded, (c) order field values are NOT hardcoded (customer names/doc text not present in JS). Executed decoded JS via page.evaluate on https://estamping-guj.preview.emergentagent.com/shcil-mock.html and captured console + registered dialog listener. The bookmarklet filled 6 of 7 fields (purBy, desc, fp, sp, duty, ddlPaidBy=Second Party); consideration remained empty only because this particular order's consideration_price is null in backend data (not a bookmarklet bug - fields with no value are skipped by design). page.on('dialog') NEVER fired. Console diagnostic output is exactly as specified: a header line 'DocGalaxy Autofill — 7 fillable field(s) detected on this page:' followed by console.table of {tag,type,name,id,label} for every detected field, then a summary line 'DocGalaxy Autofill: 6 field(s) filled.' with the matched values array. Name-based (ASP.NET substring) matching works: fields named ctl00$cph$txtPurBy / txtDesc / txtFp / txtSp / txtDuty / ddlPaidBy were correctly matched via the m.n substring hints ('purby','desc','fp','sp','duty','paidby') combined with label-synonym (sibling <td>) matching.
critical_code_review_comments: bookmarklet.js console diagnostic is well-structured: uses %c styling, console.table for field diagnostics, and a green/red summary line. Good debuggability.
n (name substring hints) in FIELD_SYNONYMS correctly handles ASP.NET cryptic names; combined label+name matching with longest-match wins is a sensible strategy.
fetch uses {cache:'no-store'} - guarantees live data (verified in previous iteration). No regression on dynamic fetch.
